walkthroughs.body_html:
Population & the Environment — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Population & the Environment brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Population & the Environment.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the replacement fertility rate?

options: Malthus
Boserup
Ehrlich
Rostow

mcqs.q: What happens in Stage 2 of the Demographic Transition Model?
options: Both birth and death rates fall sharply in Stage 2.
Birth rates rise rapidly because people want larger families.
Death rates fall rapidly (due to better food, sanitation and medicine) while birth rates remain high, causing rapid population growth.
The DTM only applies to countries with more than 50 million people.

mcqs.q: Why is an ageing population a challenge for HICs?
options: Because old people consume too much food.
The DTM only applies to countries with more than 50 million people.
Rising dependency ratio means fewer workers support more pensioners through tax, increasing pressure on pensions, healthcare and social care services.
Because old people stop contributing anything to society.

mcqs.q: Why is the Demographic Transition Model criticised for not applying to all countries?
options: It was based on European industrialisation. LICs today face different conditions: imported medicine without industrialisation, cultural factors, gender inequality and globalised economies — not all follow the same path.
The DTM only applies to countries with more than 50 million people.
All countries follow the five stages of the DTM in order.
Both birth and death rates fall sharply in Stage 2.
